name: Far-Field Speaker Recognition Benchmark (DiPCo)
description: In this paper, we present a far-field speaker verification benchmark derived from the publicly-available DiPCo corpus. This corpus comprise three different tasks that involve enrollment and test conditions with single- and/or multi-channels recordings. The main goal of this corpus is to foster research in far-field and multi-channel text-independent speaker verification. Also, it can be used for other speaker recognition tasks such as dereverberation, denoising and speech enhancement. In addition, we release a Kaldi and SpeechBrain system to facilitate further research. And we validate the evaluation design with a single-microphone state-of-the-art speaker recognition system (i.e. ResNet-101). The results show that the proposed tasks are very challenging. And we hope these resources will inspire the speech community to develop new methods and systems for this challenging domain.
evaluation_method: EER (equal error rate) and minDCF (detection cost function)
reputation: A recognized, challenging benchmark in the speech community for far-field and multi-channel speaker recognition, accompanied by Kaldi and SpeechBrain recipes.
notes: Designed for far-field, multi-channel recordings; tasks are intentionally challenging; useful also for dereverberation/denoising research; not an LLM benchmark.
